mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 0.5% signals strengthening labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 4.8% in a single month, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer confidence and spending, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 4.8%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals tightening monetary policy coinciding with manufacturing contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (FEDFUNDS up and INDPRO down) fails to predict negative returns in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion regimes characterized by high consumer credit (RSAFS) above 350,000 million dollars and rising housing starts (HOUST) above 1600 thousand units, the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to overvaluation and impending monetary tightening, producing negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In the late-cycle expansion regime (RSAFS > 350,000 and HOUST > 1600), SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (index 2017=100) indicates manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate profits and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO falls below 100.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.0% signals persistent inflation that typically leads to higher interest rates and negative equity returns, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL growth exceeds 2.0% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1500 thousand units, it signals a weakening housing market that reduces consumer wealth and spending, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when HOUST falls below 1500.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in consumer credit (RSAFS) below 350,000 million dollars and housing starts (HOUST) below 1600 thousand units indicates contraction in consumer spending and housing activity, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (RSAFS down and HOUST down) fails to predict negative returns in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.
